prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. WD-ZOE / Zoe: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. Kit and Zoe have equal standing height. Include only characters needed by this exact scene, not every reference pose. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: The Swapping Clips; World Discovery; fiction.
Setting: Ordinary classroom play table. Explicit fantasy: two silver clips connected by one green cord exchange only the overall colors of the two clipped objects; nothing changes size, shape or ownership. Clips themselves and people never change color. Each exchange happens once when the second clip is fastened; removing and fastening the pair again reverses it. The colors do not keep oscillating while clips remain attached.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Two silver spring clips joined by a green cord; One plain blue wooden toy cart, becoming red after swaps; Zoe’s plain red cup, briefly blue then restored; One red sheet of paper, ultimately blue
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: Before first swap: cup red, cart blue, paper red; clips still free, silver; cord green.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Kit holds two connected silver clips beside Zoe’s red cup and his blue cart, ready to attach them. The red paper lies unused farther back. Continuity: Before first swap: cup red, cart blue, paper red; clips still free, silver; cord green.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions.

visualReview.note: Blue cart with wooden wheels, red handled cup/sheet, silver clip pair and green cord; initial color states and classroom inspected.
visualReview.limits: Direct agent image/sequence inspection; not physical classroom observation.
